definitions.explanation: A large gathering of people, often in a public space. Can be neutral or carry negative connotations of an uncontrolled or anonymous mass.

examples.japanese: {群衆|ぐんしゅう}が{広場|ひろば}に{集|あつ}まった。
examples.english: A crowd gathered in the plaza.

examples.japanese: {群衆|ぐんしゅう}の{中|なか}で{迷子|まいご}になりそうだった。
examples.english: I almost got lost in the crowd.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}は{興奮|こうふん}した{群衆|ぐんしゅう}を{抑|おさ}えるのに{苦労|くろう}した。
examples.english: The police struggled to control the agitated crowd.

notes:
A somewhat formal or literary word for a large gathering of people. In everyday speech, {人込|ひとご}み or {人|ひと}だかり are more common for neutral crowds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {群衆|ぐんしゅう}が{集|あつ}まる (a crowd gathers)
- {群衆|ぐんしゅう}に{紛|まぎ}れる (to blend into the crowd)
- {群衆|ぐんしゅう}{心理|しんり} (mob mentality)

USAGE NOTE:
{群衆|ぐんしゅう} often appears in news reports and literary contexts. It can imply an anonymous, faceless mass and is commonly used when describing demonstrations, riots, or large public events.
